---
title: "LargeST traffic flow over OpenStreetMap roads"
output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: true
params:
  snapshot: "data/largest-visualization.json.gz"
  time_index: 97
  output_dir: "output/largest-0800"
---

This example is an **offline reproduction bundle**: the `data/` folder contains
the complete saved traffic snapshot (288 five-minute frames), downloaded OSM
roads, water and place labels, and the source archive, tile checksums, dates and provenance of the downloads.
Keep this folder, `osm-figures.R` and this R Markdown together. Install `bdynets`,
`jsonlite`, `knitr` and `rmarkdown` once. Knitting requires no network, original
HTML, HDF5 files, model fitting or browser execution.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(bdynets)
source("osm-figures.R")
stopifnot(file.exists(params$snapshot))
snapshot <- read_traffic_data(params$snapshot)
stopifnot(snapshot$source == "largest")
```

## Morning traffic in geographic context

The default is **08:00 on July 31, 2019** (one-based frame 97). Thin gray lines
show downloaded OSM major roads from the zoom-9 basemap. Colored lines retain the original traffic display links, source quantile
thresholds and directional offsets; these links are **not map-matched road
segments or inferred network adjacency**. The background is a contemporary OSM
extract, not a reconstruction of the road network in 2019. Both layers use Web
Mercator. Labels are thinned for readability.

```{r maps, fig.width=c(10,7), fig.height=c(8,9), out.width='100%'}
frames <- largest_osm_figures(snapshot, time_index=params$time_index)
```

Each region uses its own saved quantile thresholds: the same color need not
mean the same flow in the two regions. Missing flow is gray. Values retain the
source visualization's saved precision; display-link values are endpoint
averages and should not be treated as independent sensor counts.

## Export figures and retain the selected data

This executable chunk creates a real relative directory, including parents,
and checks that it is writable before opening graphics devices. Re-knitting
replaces this example's named exports. Change `output_dir` to preserve a run.

```{r export}
largest_osm_figures(snapshot, time_index=params$time_index,
                    output_dir=params$output_dir)
list.files(params$output_dir)
```

Exports include PDF, high-resolution PNG, selected frames as RDS, input checksums
and session information. The full traffic time series and OSM-derived responses stay
in `data/`, so other time frames can be reproduced offline.

```{r other-time, eval=FALSE}
# Original viewer default: 16:10, one-based frame 195.
largest_osm_figures(snapshot, time_index=195L,
                    output_dir="output/largest-1610")
```

## Data provenance

Map data © [OpenStreetMap contributors](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright),
available under ODbL 1.0. The cached display geometry comes from the October 12, 2026
[Protomaps build](https://docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/downloads), an OSM-derived
basemap distributed as an ODbL Produced Work. Geometry is simplified at zoom 9
and split at tile boundaries; it is suitable for map context, not routing or
raw OSM network analysis. Water and place labels are cached too.
`download_osm.py` documents the one-time download and skips existing extracts;
normal rendering never calls it. To refresh deliberately, archive the old OSM
files and run the script with Python 3, `pmtiles`, `mapbox-vector-tile`, `requests` and
internet access. Daily upstream archives may expire; the committed local extracts
are the reproducible source for these figures.

```{r provenance}
snapshot$provenance
lapply(list.files("data",pattern="osm-provenance.json$",full.names=TRUE),
       function(path) {
         p <- jsonlite::fromJSON(path)
         p[c("source_url", "build_date", "retrieved_utc", "zoom",
             "sha256_uncompressed", "attribution", "limitations")]
       })
lapply(snapshot$data$regions,function(region) unlist(region$breaks))
sessionInfo()
```
